adversarial_refutations.argument:
Not refuted. I attacked each model in the brief and could not exhibit a printed object excluded by the Lean structures or a Lean object excluded by the printed text.

(1) Direction loop. Printed: continuous T : ℝ/ℤ → S¹. Lean DirectionLoop (statement lines 83-87): T : ℝ → Plane, Continuous T, Function.Periodic T 1 (= ∀ x, T (x+1) = T x), ∀ s, euclideanLength (T s) = 1. Plane is `abbrev Plane := ℝ × ℝ` (work/lean/SM/Polygon.lean:13); euclideanLength u = ‖⟨u.1,u.2⟩‖_ℂ = √(u.1²+u.2²) (EuclideanPlane.lean:29-34), so the unit-length normalisation is the genuine Euclidean circle (not the sup-norm unit square of the product norm). Composing with the quotient ℝ → ℝ/ℤ (open surjection, hence quotient map) is a bijection between printed loops and 1-periodic continuous unit-length maps ℝ → ℝ²; product topology = Euclidean topology. No loop is lost either way.

(2) Seam lift. Printed: continuous θ : [0,1] → ℝ with T(s) = (cos θ(s), sin θ(s)), 0 ≤ s ≤ 1. Lean IsSeamLift (lines 124-125): ContinuousOn θ (Icc 0 1) ∧ ∀ s ∈ Icc 0 1, T s = (cos (θ s), sin (θ s)), θ : ℝ → ℝ. ContinuousOn f s ↔ Continuous (s.restrict f) (Mathlib continuousOn_iff_continuous_restrict, Topology/ContinuousOn.lean:116), so Lean seam lifts restricted to [0,1] are exactly the printed lifts and every printed lift extends. Only θ 0, θ 1 enter tw. Pair order (cos, sin) with det u v = u.1*v.2 − u.2*v.1 is the standard orientation as printed.

(3) Lift device. tw L := (L.lift 1 − L.lift 0)/(2π) with lift := Classical.choose of a global lift (lines 154, 200). For ANY printed seam lift θ: lift|[0,1] is itself a seam lift; two seam lifts have (cos,sin)(θ₁−θ₂) = (1,0) on [0,1], so θ₁−θ₂ ∈ 2πℤ pointwise and continuous on connected [0,1], hence constant; increments agree. So tw cannot differ from the printed (θ(1)−θ(0))/2π for any printed θ. The field tw_eq (lines 303-304) asserts exactly this for every IsSeamLift, so the pin holds independently of the proof device. Factor 2*Real.pi correct.

(4) Closed C¹ regular curve. Printed: γ : ℝ/ℤ → ℝ² closed C¹ regular, γ' ≠ 0 everywhere. Lean ClosedC1Curve (lines 241-247): Periodic γ 1, ∀ t, HasDerivAt γ (γ' t) t, Continuous γ' (C¹ IS demanded), ∀ t, γ' t ≠ 0. γ' is bundled data but uniquely determined by HasDerivAt.unique (Mathlib Deriv/Basic.lean:399), so the structure is in bijection with qualifying γ. Differentiability is invariant under the equivalent sup/Euclidean norms on ℝ×ℝ. Attack via a seam corner (γ(0)=γ(1) but unequal one-sided tangents) fails on both sides: C¹ on the manifold ℝ/ℤ forces equal tangents, and Lean's two-sided HasDerivAt at every t plus periodicity forces γ' 1-periodic (deriv_periodic, lines 252-261). Curves C¹-but-not-regular or regular-but-not-C¹ are excluded by both.

(5) T_γ = normalize (γ' t) = (euclideanLength (γ' t))⁻¹ • γ' t = γ'/|γ'| (line 226); rot c = tw c.tangentLoop (274); R = |rot| for curves (277) and polygonR P = |rotationNumber P| (283). Exact.

(6) Polygon sentence. Printed: "for a polygon in the regular locus, rot remains that of Lemma lem:rot". lem:rot (reference/SM/sm-1-polygons.tex:407-408): rot(P) = (1/2π) Σ ϑ_i(P) for P ∈ 𝓡_n; def:regular (386-395) gives ϑ_i ∈ (−π,π) via cos and sign of det, 𝓡_n = all ℓ_i ≠ 0 and no ℓ_i a negative multiple of ℓ_{i−1}; def:polygon (27-45) has n ≥ 3 and ℓ_i = μ_{i+1} − μ_i. Lean: rotationNumber P = (Σ principalTurn P i)/(2π) (RotationNumber.lean:10-11), principalTurn P i = principalAngle (edge P (i−1)) (edge P i), edge P i = P (i+1) − P i (Polygon.lean:49), Regular P ↔ ∀ i, edge P i ≠ 0 ∧ ¬∃ r<0, edge P i = r • edge P (i−1) (RegularLocus.lean:12-19), PrincipalAngleSpec = the printed (−π,π)/cos/sign characterisation (PrincipalAngles.lean:9-12). The printed sentence only re-points rot at lem:rot; it does not require a polygon-to-direction-loop comparison (that is cf:lem-turnlift (iii)). Field polygon_rot (lines 319-321) with 3 ≤ n and Regular P matches def:polygon's n ≥ 3 and "in the regular locus".

Non-blocking observations (not refutations): (a) the bundle includes content printed in cf:lem-turnlift (i) rather than in the definition — exists_tangent_angle_lift, tw_integer, lift_and_seam_independent (lines 300-301, 306, 327-330); stronger than the printed definition, harmless. (b) polygonR/rotationNumber are total over all [NeZero n] and all P, so junk values exist for n<3 or non-regular P, whereas printed R(L) is only for polygons in 𝓡_n; standard total-function extension, no contradiction. (c) tangent_angle_lift (lines 295-297) is a definitional tautology over arbitrary T : ℝ → Plane. (d) The forward reference to reparametrisation invariance is not rendered (correctly left to cf:lem-turnlift (i)). None of these yields a printed direction loop or closed C¹ regular curve excluded by the Lean, a Lean object excluded by the printed text, or a printed lift θ for which tw differs from (θ(1)−θ(0))/2π.

NOT REFUTED. I attacked the polygon sentence, the R sentence, and the independence-clause boundary; each attack fails on the primitives.

1. Polygon sentence (printed line 15-16 of the excerpt: "For a polygon in the regular locus, rot remains that of Lemma lem:rot"). Content of the printed sentence: the symbol rot on polygons is NOT redefined via direction loops; it keeps lem:rot's definition rot(P) = (1/2π) Σ_{i∈ℤ/n} ϑ_i(P) for P ∈ ℛ_n (sm-1-polygons.tex:408). No polygon-to-direction-loop comparison is required or possible: a polygon is not C¹, so T_γ does not exist for it; the consumer's preamble (sm-3:3543-3545) says verbatim "rot is as in Lemma lem:rot for polygons and Definition cf:def-turning for direction loops and closed C¹ regular curves", and its proof of (ii) (sm-3:3620-3622) says "polygonal rotation was defined there by the sum of principal angles"; the corner-smoothing comparison is cf:lem-turnlift (iii), not the definition. Expanding: `rotationNumber P := (Σ_{i:ZMod n} principalTurn P i)/(2π)` (RotationNumber.lean:10-11); `principalTurn P i := principalAngle (edge P (i-1)) (edge P i)` (RegularLocus.lean:15-16); `edge P i = P(i+1) − P i` = ℓ_i (Polygon.lean:49); on a RegularPair, `principalAngle u v` satisfies `PrincipalAngleSpec`: θ ∈ (−π,π), cos θ = planeDot u v/(euclideanLength u · euclideanLength v), sign θ = sign (det u v) (PrincipalAngles.lean:9-16) — exactly def:regular's ϑ_i (sm-1:387-391); `Regular P := ∀ i, RegularPair (edge P (i-1)) (edge P i)` with `RegularPair u v := u ≠ 0 ∧ v ≠ 0 ∧ ¬∃ r<0, v = r•u` (RegularLocus.lean:12-13, RegularPairs.lean:8-9) = ℛ_n (sm-1:391-393). 3. Independence clauses. Yes, cf:lem-turnlift (i) content is present in the row: lift existence (`exists_tangent_angle_lift`, 300-301), lift-choice and seam independence (`lift_and_seam_independent`, 327-330), and tw integrality (`tw_integer`, 306; the word "integer" is only printed in lem-turnlift (i), sm-3:3548). Without them the row would be WEAKER than printed; with them it is exactly the printed value. Reparametrisation invariance is correctly excluded and documented (40-41, 325-326). So the extras are stronger-than-source, not "other", and nothing printed is omitted.

Remaining sentences checked for completeness: D1 (ℝ/ℤ→S¹ continuous ↔ 1-periodic continuous ℝ→Plane with euclideanLength = 1; euclideanLength = ‖planeComplex ·‖ is the Euclidean norm, EuclideanPlane.lean:9,29, not the sup norm of ℝ×ℝ — so S¹ is the round circle, 83-87); D2 (IsSeamLift = ContinuousOn Icc 0 1 ∧ equation on Icc 0 1, 124-125, equivalent to a continuous θ:[0,1]→ℝ); D3 (tw_eq for every seam lift); D4 (ClosedC1Curve: HasDerivAt everywhere, Continuous γ' renders C¹, γ' ≠ 0, 1-periodic, 241-247; tangentLoop.T t = (euclideanLength (γ' t))⁻¹ • γ' t, 264-271).
